answer: Future-beacon admission puzzle: an agent posts a key commitment before a threshold-randomness beacon round. Validators keep an echo of each commitment in a public log. After the beacon publishes, a verifiable random function over commitment and beacon sets a work target; admission needs a proof meeting it. The attacker cannot precompute targets, so every candidate pays an independent post-beacon hash search plus registration fee; rejected keys pay the same before retrying.
